Sweet Pineapple and Raisin Tamales

Served at: La Noche de Rabanos

Serves 8Prep 45 minCook 1 hour

Sweet Pineapple and Raisin Tamales are a festive treat traditionally enjoyed during La Noche de Rábanos, a unique Mexican holiday celebrated on December 23rd in Oaxaca. This dish combines the warmth of sweet tamales with tropical pineapple and plump raisins, embodying the holiday's spirit of creativity and community.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480 g) masa harina
  • 1 1/3 cups (320 ml) warm water
  • 1 cup (225 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 cups (300 g) fresh pineapple, finely chopped
  • 1 cup (150 g) golden raisins
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 30 dried corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Method

  1. Drain the soaked corn husks and pat them dry.
  2. In a large bowl, beat the softened butter with the sugar until creamy and fluffy.
  3. In a separate bowl, combine the masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
  4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, alternating with warm water, mixing until a soft dough forms.
  5. Incorporate the ground cinnamon, chopped pineapple, and raisins into the dough, mixing gently to distribute evenly.
  6. Spread about 2 tablespoons of the masa mixture onto the center of each corn husk, forming a rectangle about 3x4 inches.
  7. Fold the sides of the husk over the filling, then fold the bottom up and secure if needed.
  8. Place the tamales upright in a steamer basket with the open end up.
  9. Steam the tamales over boiling water for about 60 minutes, checking occasionally to ensure water doesn’t evaporate completely.
  10. Tamales are done when the dough is firm and pulls away easily from the husk.
  11. Let them cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute some of the water with pineapple juice.
  • If fresh pineapple is unavailable, use canned crushed pineapple, drained well.
  • Serve warm with a sprinkle of cinnamon sugar or a drizzle of honey for extra sweetness.
